patients.label: 48-year-old man with HIV infection, hepatoportal sclerosis and two liver lesions that proved to be hepatocellular carcinoma

identity_evidence.quote: A 48-year-old man with a 15-year history of well-controlled HIV infection

attribution_limitations: The Discussion says HPS changes were not found on the explant and offers sampling error or complete resolution after drug discontinuation as explanations, while also calling this complete remission of HPS. Resolution of HPS is therefore recorded as review-only and no mechanism or cause is inferred.

The Discussion calls the liver parenchyma biopsy diagnostic of HPS, while the Case Report calls the nonneoplastic parenchyma suggestive of HPS and the Discussion also calls HPS a presumptive diagnosis. HPS is kept provisional. The source does not say whether the Discussion's biopsy of the liver parenchyma is the targeted biopsy of the Case Report, so no separate biopsy is recorded.

Hepatic venous pressure gradient of 2 mmHg and the later statement that hepatic vein wedge pressure was within normal limits are not identified by the source as the same measurement and are kept separate.
The source does not say which of the two liver lesions corresponds to which HCC; the two tumors are recorded as one tumor item and no lesion-to-tumor mapping is inferred.

evidence.quote:
Figure 1
Noncirrhotic liver parenchyma but with significant portal hypertension including splenomegaly and varices.

Figure 2
Hepatic adenoma. Well-differentiated neoplasm composed of normal appearing hepatocytes arranged in sheets and thin cords with patchy pseudoacinar growth pattern (thin arrows), scattered inflammatory foci, and bands of fibrosis with unpaired arteries (thick arrow) (H&E, 200x).

Figure 3
Dense portal fibrosis with loss of portal veins branches (H&E and trichrome stain, 100x).

limitations: Single-patient report; the case narrative gives no calendar dates, only "Two years later" between the biopsy workup and the transplant-center visit.
HPS resolution is stated in the Discussion alongside speculation about sampling error; recorded review-only.
Source does not map the two CT lesions to the two resected carcinomas.
Caption-layer visual status not_inspected; the three JPEGs are inspected in visual.json.
